papers.authors: T. Bertin-Mahieux, D. P. W. Ellis, B. Whitman, P. Lamere
papers.title: The Million Song Dataset
papers.venue: Proc. 12th International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference (ISMIR 2011), Miami, FL, USA, pp. 591-596, 2011
papers.verified_via: https://ismir2011.ismir.net/papers/OS6-1.pdf -> HTTP 200; PDF text read (title, authors, abstract; printed page numbers 591-596)
papers.why_it_matters: It is the large-scale ancestor of the Echo Nest/Spotify-style audio descriptors (loudness, tempo, timbre) that SonicAtlas profiles across genres and eras.
papers.description: The authors release a free collection of pre-computed audio features and metadata for one million commercial popular-music tracks and describe how it was assembled and linked to other resources. As a showcase they predict a track's release year from its audio descriptors and report encouraging results.
papers.drawbacks: Raw audio is not distributed and the features are frozen Echo Nest outputs, so the paper offers a dataset rather than any exploratory or interactive analysis of it.

papers.authors: R. Panda, R. Malheiro, R. P. Paiva
papers.title: Novel Audio Features for Music Emotion Recognition
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing, vol. 11, no. 4, pp. 614-626, 2020
papers.verified_via: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1109/TAFFC.2018.2820691 -> HTTP 200 (Crossref metadata matched title/authors/venue); abstract read via OpenAlex
papers.why_it_matters: It links low-level audio descriptors to perceived emotion, which helps interpret Spotify's valence and energy fields that SonicAtlas maps.
papers.description: The work audits which musical concepts existing feature extractors miss and proposes new descriptors for texture and expressive technique, evaluated on a new 900-clip dataset labelled by Russell's emotion quadrants. Adding the new features raised the F1-score of emotion classification by roughly nine points over a baseline-only feature set.
papers.drawbacks: The dataset is small (900 clips) and focused on classification accuracy; it does not study genre or decade trends and provides no exploratory tool.

papers.authors: G. Tzanetakis, P. Cook
papers.title: Musical genre classification of audio signals
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Speech and Audio Processing, vol. 10, no. 5, pp. 293-302, Jul. 2002
papers.verified_via: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1109/TSA.2002.800560 -> HTTP 200 (Crossref metadata matched title/authors/venue); abstract read via OpenAlex
papers.why_it_matters: It is the canonical baseline showing that hand-crafted timbre, rhythm and pitch features separate genres, the same premise behind SonicAtlas's genre comparisons.
papers.description: The paper proposes three feature families describing timbral texture, rhythmic content and pitch content, and uses them to classify audio into a hierarchy of genres. It analyses how much each feature set contributes and introduced the dataset later known as GTZAN.
papers.drawbacks: It works on a few hundred short clips and reports classifier accuracy only, with no temporal (era) analysis, lyrics, or interactive exploration.

papers.authors: K. Choi, G. Fazekas, M. Sandler, K. Cho
papers.title: Convolutional recurrent neural networks for music classification
papers.venue: Proc. 2017 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP), New Orleans, LA, USA, pp. 2392-2396, 2017
papers.verified_via: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1109/ICASSP.2017.7952585 -> HTTP 200 (Crossref metadata matched title/authors/venue); abstract read via OpenAlex
papers.why_it_matters: It represents the deep-learning route to genre/tag prediction that SonicAtlas contrasts with its transparent, feature-level EDA.
papers.description: The authors combine convolutional layers for local feature extraction with recurrent layers that summarise the sequence over time for music tagging. Compared with three CNN designs at matched parameter counts, the hybrid model gave strong accuracy for its size and training cost.
papers.drawbacks: The models learn opaque representations from spectrograms, which makes it hard to explain which musical properties drive a genre label, and no exploratory interface is offered.

papers.authors: B. L. Sturm
papers.title: The GTZAN dataset: Its contents, its faults, their effects on evaluation, and its future use
papers.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:1306.1461, 2013
papers.verified_via: https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.1461 -> HTTP 200 (citation_title/author/abstract meta tags read)
papers.why_it_matters: It warns that genre datasets contain duplicates and mislabels, motivating the data-quality and duplicate checks SonicAtlas runs before comparing genres.
papers.description: Sturm catalogues the repetitions, mislabelled excerpts and distortions in GTZAN and surveys how often prior work used it without noticing. He shows the faults change the evaluation of several genre-recognition systems in different ways and argues for careful rather than blind use of the dataset.
papers.drawbacks: It is a critique of one small benchmark and does not provide tools for auditing large Spotify-scale tables interactively.

papers.authors: M. Interiano, K. Kazemi, L. Wang, J. Yang, Z. Yu, N. L. Komarova
papers.title: Musical trends and predictability of success in contemporary songs in and out of the top charts
papers.venue: Royal Society Open Science, vol. 5, no. 5, Art. no. 171274, 2018
papers.verified_via: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1098/rsos.171274 -> HTTP 200 (Crossref metadata matched title/authors/venue); abstract read in Crossref record
papers.why_it_matters: It is the closest prior study to SonicAtlas, tracking acoustic descriptors across three decades and relating them to chart success.
papers.description: Using over half a million UK releases from 1985-2015, the authors find long-term declines in 'happiness' and 'brightness' and a small rise in 'sadness', while chart hits tend to be happier, more party-like and less relaxed than typical releases. They then train random-forest models on acoustic features to estimate how predictable chart success is.
papers.drawbacks: Findings are reported as static figures for one market, without lyrics content or an interactive environment for others to re-slice the data.

papers.authors: N. Askin, M. Mauskapf
papers.title: What Makes Popular Culture Popular? Product Features and Optimal Differentiation in Music
papers.venue: American Sociological Review, vol. 82, no. 5, pp. 910-944, Oct. 2017
papers.verified_via: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1177/0003122417728662 -> HTTP 200 (Crossref metadata matched title/authors/venue); abstract read in Crossref record
papers.why_it_matters: It shows that a song's position in audio-feature space relative to its peers matters for success, supporting SonicAtlas's similarity-map view.
papers.description: Building audio-feature profiles for about 27,000 Billboard Hot 100 songs, the authors test whether feature-space typicality predicts chart performance beyond artist and label effects. They find that songs that are somewhat, but not overly, distinct from contemporaries do best.
papers.drawbacks: The analysis is a regression study on chart songs only, so non-hits, lyrics and interactive exploration are outside its scope.

papers.authors: D. Herremans, D. Martens, K. Sörensen
papers.title: Dance Hit Song Prediction
papers.venue: Journal of New Music Research, vol. 43, no. 3, pp. 291-302, 2014
papers.verified_via: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1080/09298215.2014.881888 -> HTTP 200 (Crossref metadata matched title/authors/venue); abstract read via OpenAlex
papers.why_it_matters: It is a reference point for using audio descriptors to separate hits from non-hits within a single genre, a slice SonicAtlas can reproduce.
papers.description: The authors assemble dance chart songs from 1985 to 2013 with basic and temporally aware audio features and compare several classifiers. Their best model distinguishes top-10 dance hits from lower-ranked entries reasonably well.
papers.drawbacks: It covers only one genre and frames popularity as binary classification, offering no cross-genre, cross-era or lyrics perspective.

papers.authors: J. Serrà, Á. Corral, M. Boguñá, M. Haro, J. Ll. Arcos
papers.title: Measuring the Evolution of Contemporary Western Popular Music
papers.venue: Scientific Reports, vol. 2, Art. no. 521, Jul. 2012
papers.verified_via: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1038/srep00521 -> HTTP 200 (Crossref metadata matched title/authors/venue); abstract read via OpenAlex
papers.why_it_matters: It provides the headline 'louder and more homogeneous' finding that SonicAtlas can check with Spotify loudness and timbre-like features by decade.
papers.description: Analysing pitch, timbre and loudness descriptors over more than fifty years of Western pop, the authors find many statistical regularities are stable. They nonetheless report narrower pitch transitions, a more uniform timbral palette and steadily rising loudness.
papers.drawbacks: It relies on Million Song Dataset descriptors and static plots, without genre-level breakdowns, lyrics, or an interactive way to verify the trends.

papers.authors: M. Mauch, R. M. MacCallum, M. Levy, A. M. Leroi
papers.title: The evolution of popular music: USA 1960-2010
papers.venue: Royal Society Open Science, vol. 2, no. 5, Art. no. 150081, 2015
papers.verified_via: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1098/rsos.150081 -> HTTP 200 (Crossref metadata matched title/authors/venue); abstract read in Crossref record
papers.why_it_matters: It models stylistic change and diversity across decades, directly informing SonicAtlas's era-level comparisons and change-point view.
papers.description: Studying about 17,000 Billboard Hot 100 recordings, the authors extract harmonic and timbral topics, cluster songs into audio-based styles and measure diversity over time. They test classic theories of cultural change against measured diversity and find that evolution was largely continuous yet interrupted by a small number of rapid stylistic shifts.
papers.drawbacks: Only US chart songs from 30-second previews are used and results are static; lyrics and non-chart music are not examined.

papers.authors: C. Hutto, E. Gilbert
papers.title: VADER: A Parsimonious Rule-Based Model for Sentiment Analysis of Social Media Text
papers.venue: Proc. International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media (ICWSM), vol. 8, no. 1, pp. 216-225, 2014
papers.verified_via: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1609/icwsm.v8i1.14550 -> HTTP 200 (Crossref metadata matched title/authors/venue); abstract read in Crossref record
papers.why_it_matters: VADER is a lightweight lexicon scorer suitable for computing lyric sentiment over many songs, one of the options SonicAtlas uses or compares against TextBlob.
papers.description: The authors build and validate a sentiment lexicon with intensity scores and add grammatical rules for cues such as negation, capitalisation and punctuation. The resulting model rivals or beats eleven established lexicon and machine-learning baselines on short social-media text.
papers.drawbacks: It was tuned on tweets and reviews, not poetic or slang-heavy lyrics, and handles only English, so lyric scores need caution.

papers.authors: C. O. Brand, A. Acerbi, A. Mesoudi
papers.title: Cultural evolution of emotional expression in 50 years of song lyrics
papers.venue: Evolutionary Human Sciences, vol. 1, Art. no. e11, 2019
papers.verified_via: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1017/ehs.2019.11 -> HTTP 200 (Crossref metadata matched title/authors/venue); abstract read on Cambridge Core landing page (doi.org redirect, HTTP 200)
papers.why_it_matters: It documents rising negativity in pop lyrics over 1965-2015, a trend SonicAtlas can test against lyric sentiment by decade.
papers.description: Using two lyric corpora (about 4,900 chart songs and 159,000 songs) spanning 1965-2015, the authors test whether cultural-transmission biases explain the growth of negative emotional content. Negative lyrics fare somewhat better in charts, but much of the trend is explained by unbiased copying of past frequencies.
papers.drawbacks: Audio features are not considered alongside the text, and the study is a modelling paper with no exploratory interface. Note: it appeared in Evolutionary Human Sciences, not Scientific Reports.

papers.authors: M. Fell, C. Sporleder
papers.title: Lyrics-based Analysis and Classification of Music
papers.venue: Proc. COLING 2014, the 25th International Conference on Computational Linguistics: Technical Papers, Dublin, Ireland, pp. 620-631, Aug. 2014
papers.verified_via: https://aclanthology.org/C14-1059/ -> HTTP 200 (ACL Anthology record; abstract read from the PDF https://aclanthology.org/C14-1059.pdf)
papers.why_it_matters: Its stylistic lyric features (vocabulary, style, semantics, structure) suggest which text statistics SonicAtlas can profile per genre and era.
papers.description: The authors design lyric features capturing vocabulary, style, semantics, world orientation and song structure and combine them with n-gram models. The combination improves three tasks: genre detection, separating best from worst songs, and estimating publication period.
papers.drawbacks: It uses lyrics only, ignoring audio features, and reports classification results rather than exploratory visual analysis.

papers.authors: A. van den Oord, S. Dieleman, B. Schrauwen
papers.title: Deep content-based music recommendation
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 26 (NIPS 2013), 2013
papers.verified_via: https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2013/hash/b3ba8f1bee1238a2f37603d90b58898d-Abstract.html -> HTTP 200 (title, authors and abstract read)
papers.why_it_matters: It motivates content-based similarity from audio, which SonicAtlas offers as a nearest-neighbour 'songs like this' view over Spotify features.
papers.description: To tackle the cold-start problem, the authors predict collaborative-filtering latent factors directly from audio, comparing bag-of-words audio features with deep CNNs on the Million Song Dataset. Predicted factors yield sensible recommendations and CNNs clearly outperform the traditional pipeline.
papers.drawbacks: It targets recommendation accuracy with learned black-box embeddings, not interpretable exploration of features, and uses no lyrics.

papers.authors: M. Schedl, H. Zamani, C.-W. Chen, Y. Deldjoo, M. Elahi
papers.title: Current challenges and visions in music recommender systems research
papers.venue: International Journal of Multimedia Information Retrieval, vol. 7, no. 2, pp. 95-116, Jun. 2018
papers.verified_via: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1007/s13735-018-0154-2 -> HTTP 200 (Crossref metadata matched title/authors/venue); abstract read via OpenAlex
papers.why_it_matters: It frames why richer content descriptors (audio, lyrics, context) matter for music discovery, positioning SonicAtlas's multimodal EDA as groundwork.
papers.description: This survey identifies the most pressing open problems for music recommenders from academic and industry viewpoints and reviews the state of the art for each. It then outlines future directions centred on listener intent, context and going beyond simple user-item signals.
papers.drawbacks: As a survey it offers no new data analysis or tool; it discusses recommender evaluation rather than exploratory understanding of catalogues.

papers.authors: L. van der Maaten, G. Hinton
papers.title: Visualizing Data using t-SNE
papers.venue: Journal of Machine Learning Research, vol. 9, no. 86, pp. 2579-2605, 2008
papers.verified_via: https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v9/vandermaaten08a.html -> HTTP 200 (citation meta tags and abstract read)
papers.why_it_matters: t-SNE is one of the embedding options for SonicAtlas's 2-D 'sound map' of tracks.
papers.description: The authors present a variant of Stochastic Neighbor Embedding that is easier to optimise and reduces the crowding of points in the map centre. It reveals structure at several scales and outperforms methods such as Sammon mapping, Isomap and LLE on many datasets.
papers.drawbacks: Distances between clusters and global layout are not reliable, and the method scales poorly to millions of points without approximation, so maps need careful reading.

papers.authors: S. T. Roweis, L. K. Saul
papers.title: Nonlinear Dimensionality Reduction by Locally Linear Embedding
papers.verified_via: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1126/science.290.5500.2323 -> HTTP 200 (Crossref metadata matched title/authors/venue); abstract read in Crossref record
papers.why_it_matters: LLE is a classic manifold-learning baseline that SonicAtlas can cite when justifying non-linear maps over PCA.
papers.description: LLE reconstructs each point from its neighbours with linear weights and then finds a low-dimensional embedding that preserves those weights. Because it avoids local minima and keeps neighbourhoods, it recovers the global structure of non-linear manifolds such as face images and text.
papers.drawbacks: It is sensitive to the neighbourhood size and noise and is rarely used at the scale of million-track catalogues.

papers.authors: L. McInnes, J. Healy, J. Melville
papers.title: UMAP: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection for Dimension Reduction
papers.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:1802.03426, 2018
papers.verified_via: https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03426 -> HTTP 200 (citation meta tags and abstract read)
papers.why_it_matters: UMAP is a fast, scalable choice for precomputing the 2-D track map that SonicAtlas ships to the browser.
papers.description: UMAP derives a manifold-learning algorithm from Riemannian geometry and algebraic topology and turns it into a practical, scalable method. It matches t-SNE's visual quality, arguably keeps more global structure, runs faster and supports any embedding dimension.
papers.drawbacks: Embeddings depend on hyperparameters and random seeds and are still not distance-faithful, so cluster positions must not be over-interpreted.

papers.authors: I. T. Jolliffe, J. Cadima
papers.title: Principal component analysis: a review and recent developments
papers.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences, vol. 374, no. 2065, Art. no. 20150202, Apr. 2016
papers.verified_via: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1098/rsta.2015.0202 -> HTTP 200 (Crossref metadata matched title/authors/venue); abstract read in Crossref record
papers.why_it_matters: PCA gives SonicAtlas an interpretable linear baseline, with loadings that explain which audio features drive the map axes.
papers.description: The review explains how PCA builds uncorrelated components that successively capture maximum variance via an eigen-decomposition. It then surveys adaptations of PCA for different data types and structures and discusses what the method can and cannot do.
papers.drawbacks: Being linear, PCA can miss non-linear genre structure that t-SNE or UMAP reveal; the paper is methodological and has no music application.

papers.authors: T. Milo, A. Somech
papers.title: Automating Exploratory Data Analysis via Machine Learning: An Overview
papers.venue: Proc. 2020 ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data, Portland, OR, USA, pp. 2617-2622, 2020

papers.description: This tutorial-style overview reviews the many systems built over the past decade to ease EDA, an iterative process of filtering, aggregating and visualising unfamiliar data. It organises them around how machine learning is used to recommend or automate the next analysis steps.
papers.drawbacks: It is a survey for database researchers and is domain-agnostic, so it gives no guidance on music data or on running EDA fully in the browser.

papers.authors: K. Wongsuphasawat, D. Moritz, A. Anand, J. Mackinlay, B. Howe, J. Heer

papers.drawbacks: It is a general tool evaluated on small tables, not tuned for million-row music datasets or text features like lyrics.

papers.description: The demo introduces DuckDB, an in-process database built for analytical SQL in the way SQLite serves transactional workloads. The authors benchmark it against other data-management systems in embedded-analytics scenarios and release it as open source.

papers.authors: J. Heer, D. Moritz

papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics, vol. 30, no. 1, 2024 (early access 2023)

Benchmarks show order-of-magnitude speed-ups over prior web visualisation systems, enabling real-time exploration of billion-row data.
papers.drawbacks: It is a general architecture without domain analyses; it offers no ready-made EDA workflow for audio features or lyrics.

papers.authors: A. Satyanarayan, D. Moritz, K. Wongsuphasawat, J. Heer

papers.drawbacks: Rendering all data client-side becomes slow for very large tables unless paired with a database backend, and it provides no automated EDA logic.
